subject: english_beehive
question_text: Where does the traveller find himself? What problem does he face?
answer_text: The traveller finds himself in the yellow woods at a point where the road forks into two. The problem that he faces is that he cannot decide which road to take to continue his journey since it is not possible for him to travel both roads at the same time.
final_answer: The traveller is at a fork in the road and must choose one path to continue his journey.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the poem's setting and the traveller's dilemma.

subject: english_beehive
question_text: Is there any difference between the two roads as the poet describes them (i) in stanzas two and three? (ii) in the last two lines of the poem?

parts.part_text: In stanza two the poet explains that the only difference between the two roads was that the road he took had the right to be chosen (the better claim) because it was covered with grass and looked as if it had not been used too much. Besides this difference, both roads had been equally worn down by passersby travelling on them. In stanza three the poet says that both the roads were equally covered with leaves and that no person had stepped on.
parts.answer_text: In stanza two, the only difference was that the road he took had the better claim because it was covered with grass.
parts.final_answer: In stanza three, both roads were equally covered with leaves.

parts.part_text: In the last two lines of the poem the poet says that there is a difference between the two roads because he took the road that was less travelled by other people and that made all the difference to his journey.
parts.answer_text: In the last two lines, the poet indicates a difference because he took the road less travelled.
parts.final_answer: This choice made all the difference to his journey.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires analysis of the poem's stanzas and concluding lines.

subject: english_beehive
question_text: What do you think the last two lines of the poem mean? (Looking back, does the poet regret his choice or accept it?)
answer_text: The last two lines of the poem mean the acceptance of reality. The poet made a choice and accepted the challenging path. He took an unexplored path in his life. He wanted to do something different in his life so he chooses the less travelled road. No he does not regret his choice.
final_answer: The poet accepts his choice and does not regret it.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves interpretation of the poet's feelings and acceptance of choices.

subject: english_beehive
question_text: Have you ever had to make a difficult choice (or do you think you will have difficult choices to make)? How will you make the choice (for what reasons)?
answer_text: No, till now I have never been in a situation in which I had to make a difficult choice. Perhaps I am still too young to make an independent choice. Yes, I think later or sooner I will have difficult choices to make. After completing my general education, I will have to make choice of profession whether I should become an engineer or doctor or something else. I will have hundreds of options before me. Then it will be difficult to make a choice in between them. I will make choice according to my capabilities and strong points at that time. I will choose a path that gives me satisfaction and mental peace. I will not join the rat race for money. Like the poet in the poem, I will choose a challenging and unexplored path in my life.
final_answer: I will choose a path that gives me satisfaction and mental peace.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires personal reflection and understanding of future choices.

subject: english_beehive
question_text: After you have made a choice do you always think about what might have been, or do you accept the reality?
answer_text: Taking a decision sometimes makes or mars our future. Having made a choice, I accept the reality. Reconsidering a decision or contemplating over it is not a positive approach towards life. Such thoughts never allow us to be happy with what we have gained from our decision. Therefore, I believe in sticking to my decisions.
final_answer: I believe in sticking to my decisions.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding the impact of decisions on personal happiness.
